newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia noon rubber up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia noon rubber up on technical rebound.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were were quoted higher at noon as the market retained its technical firmness from last week, but consumer demand was still lacking, traders said.
"It's been a quiet morning, but that's not unusual for a Monday," said a trader.
Sales could, however, improve this week if Malaysian rubber remained at a discount against Thai material, traders said.
"(The) Bangkok (market) is currently quite expensive and consumers may buy here instead. But the question is whether they need any fresh orders," said another trader.

Traders said recent sales in the market were only for short-covering done by local and London-based agents to honour earlier bookings. Another trader said on Friday that order books of most European and U.S. buyers were full until the third quarter of 1997.
At midday, June RSS 1 buyer was officially quoted at 278.50 cents ($1.11) a kg , up half cent from Friday's close. June SMR 20 buyer also rose half cent to an official 263 cents.
Traders quoted the SMR20 at 261, SMR CV at 332, SMR 5 at 272, SMR L at 307, SMR 10 at 262.50 and drum latex at 227.
